{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox college sports team season | team = Duke Blue Devils | year = 2024–25 | sport = basketball | logo = Duke Blue Devils basketball mark.svg | logo_size = 125 | conference = Atlantic Coast Conference | short_conf = ACC | record = 35–4 | conf_record = 19–1 | CoachRank = 3 | APRank = 3 | champion = [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC regular season]] and [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|tournament]] champions | tourney = [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Final Four | captain = | head_coach = [[Jon Scheyer]] | hc_year = 3rd | assoc_coach = [[Chris Carrawell]] | asst_coach2 = [[Jai Lucas]] | asst_coach3 = [[William Avery (basketball)|Will Avery]] | asst_coach4 = Emanuel Dildy | stadium = [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] }} {{2024–25 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Blue Devils were led by third-year head coach [[Jon Scheyer]] and featured the first Duke roster with no regular rotation players from the [[Mike Krzyzewski]] era. The Blue Devils played their home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). The Blue Devils started the season ranked seventh and comfortably defeated [[2024–25 Maine Black Bears men's basketball team|Maine]] and [[2024–25 Army Black Knights men's basketball team|Army]] to open the season. They lost to nineteenth-ranked [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in the [[Champions Classic]] before holding [[2024–25 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team|Wofford]] to 35 points in a fifty one-point victory. The Kentucky defeat saw them fall to number twelve in the rankings, where they defeated seventeenth-ranked [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] 69–55. They then lost to top-ranked [[2024–25 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] 75–72 in the [[Vegas Showdown (basketball)|Vegas Showdown]]. They rose to ninth for the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] where they defeated second-ranked [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]]. This victory was the second in what would be a sixteen-game winning streak for the Blue Devils. They rose from eleventh in the rankings at the start, to second in the rankings over the sixteen wins. Twelve of the wins were conference wins and all the victories were by double-digits except a 63–56 victory over [[2024–25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] on January 25. The streak was broken by a 77–71 loss at [[2024–25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] on February 8. That loss would be the Blue Devils' only ACC loss of the season as they won the rest of their regular season games. They finished the season on an eight-game winning streak, with all their wins coming by at least thirteen points. Their regular season included a two game sweep of [[Duke–North Carolina rivalry|rivals]] [[2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. Duke did not play a ranked opponent during the ACC regular season, and finished the regular season ranked first in the polls. The Blue Devils finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|regular season]] 28–3 and 19–1 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish as regular season champions for the twenty-first time. As the first seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]] earned a bye into Quarterfinals where they defeated eighth seed [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] 78–70. In the Semifinals they faced fifth-seed North Carolina for a third time this season. The Blue Devils won the closest rivalry game of the season 74–71. In the Final, they defeated second seed and thirteenth-ranked [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] 73–62 to win their twenty-second ACC tournament title. The Blue Devils received the ACC's automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. They were a one-seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#East regional – Newark, New Jersey|East region]]. They defeated sixteen-seed [[2024–25 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]] 93–49 in the First Round, nine-seed [[2024–25 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] 89–66 in the Second Round, and won a rematch with four-seed and twenty first-ranked Arizona 100–93 in the Sweet Sixteen. They faced two-seed and seventh-ranked [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] in the Elite Eight and prevailed 85–65 to advance to the Final Four. There they were bested by the Midwest region top seed and second-ranked [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] 70–67. They finished the season with a 35–4 overall record. == Previous season == {{main|2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team}} The Blue Devils finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 27–9 and 15–5 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in second place. As the second seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they earned a bye to the quarterfinals where they were upset by in-state rival and tenth seed [[2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] where they were the fourth seed in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South regional – Dallas, Texas|South Region]]. They faced [[2023–24 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] in the first round. They won this matchup to move onto the round of 32, where they routed 12th seed [[2023–24 James Madison Dukes men's basketball team|James Madison]]. Duke then faced the number one seed, [[2023–24 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]], whom they defeated 54–51, advancing to the Elite Eight for the first time under head coach Jon Scheyer.
